prize_parts.citation: for establishing induced proximity to E3 ubiquitin ligases as a chemical design principle for targeted protein degradation, through bifunctional PROTACs and the molecular-glue mechanism of cereblon

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1 the case is stronger, because five members converge on the same three names and nobody disputes the quantitative mechanism. Ternary-complex formation, cooperativity, ubiquitin transfer and cereblon-dependent substrate recruitment have all been measured in vitro and reproduced by many independent laboratories, so the principle does not rest on any single group's data. As an experimentalist I apply this standard to maturity: has the key claim survived independent quantitative testing, and has it given other scientists a general capability? Degraders pass both tests. Approved cereblon-dependent glue drugs show that the mechanism works in patients, and the heterobifunctional arm is supported by broad replication. The chemistry is the reaction itself: a small molecule makes a new ligase-substrate pair and thereby makes a protein a substrate for ubiquitination. The citation can state that without naming a drug. Crews and Deshaies are the origin of the PROTAC concept and its first demonstration, and Handa identified cereblon, which turned the glue branch from a clinical puzzle into a defined mechanism.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved yet, so for the heterobifunctional arm the clinical consequence is a trajectory, not a settled record. This is the strongest objection, and a committee that wants the first approval first can defend waiting. The prize also joins two lines with partly different histories, and a three-person limit leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito. Sakamoto and Kim co-authored the 2001 proof of concept, and Ito is inseparable from Handa on cereblon. The omissions will have to be justified in the reports and not just asserted. Finally, some of the visible success is pharmacology, so the citation must be worded around the chemical principle.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved B026 up from fourth to preferred, but names the missing PROTAC approval and the partial separation of the glue and PROTAC arms as the main weaknesses, and warns against letting enthusiasm for a drug-discovery field displace the mechanism-level work in B028.
responses.response: I share your worry about enthusiasm, and that is why I apply a measurement test and not a count of supporters. On that test B026 does well: the physical content you value, ternary-complex thermodynamics, binding kinetics and structure, is quantified directly, and it does not wait for an approval. On the split, I would resist reading two arms as two discoveries. Both are the same event, a small molecule inducing a new E3-substrate contact, and Handa's cereblon work shows the glue arm obeys it. I still hold my round-1 doubt about B028. Gray and Winkler's work is a rigorous, kinetically tested mechanism, but I do not see how it changed the practice of other scientists beyond the Marcus-theory framework already recognised in 1992. So I keep your first choice as a strong candidate for later, not for this year.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B060 (Buchwald and Hartwig), cites clean two-person attribution and three decades of confirmation, lists B026 as his first alternative, and concedes that B026 is a genuinely new modality with stronger backing, though he questions whether its core chemistry is only ligand and linker design on known E3 ligands.
responses.response: I accept the merit and maturity of C-N coupling, and I defer to you on the synthetic side. On whether degraders are chemistry, I think linker and ligand design describes how a PROTAC is built and not what it does. What is new is the reaction it enables, induced ubiquitination of a chosen protein. That reaction has a measurable cooperative equilibrium and a defined catalytic turnover, so it can be treated as chemistry and not only as biology. The cereblon branch also shows a very simple molecule, with no designed linker, creating a new ligase surface and so acting as a reagent for a new reaction. On B060 versus the 2010 prize, I see your own point: it is mature and well attributed, but I read it as the extension of a paradigm already honoured. I would ask you, as the person closest to it, whether you could support B026 in a final configuration if the citation names the induced-proximity principle and not drugs.

responses.point: Aqvist wants the prize to be for the chemical principle and not for drugs, accepts that Sakamoto, Kim, Ciulli and Ito are hard exclusions, and said earlier that he would hear a case for Ciulli replacing Deshaies.
responses.response: I agree that the citation must rest on the principle and I have worded it that way. On Ciulli, I do not think he should replace Deshaies or Handa. Deshaies co-originated the PROTAC concept and its first demonstration, and Handa's cereblon work is the foundation of the glue arm. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the field rational and are decisive for its current practice, but they build on a concept already shown to work. I would put that extension in the expert reports as a recognised omission, and not give up a place on the concept or the mechanism. The case for Sakamoto and Kim is real. I do not see a way to include them without breaking the three-person limit, so the exclusion has to be explained in the reports and not hidden.

responses.point: Linke prefers B026 with the same three names, treats the missing PROTAC approval as the strongest objection, and has moved B067 from lead to fall-back.
responses.response: Your treatment of maturity is the fair one, and my answer to the chair's first question is that I apply a mechanism standard: independent quantitative reproduction plus an approved drug class whose action is explained by the same principle. Approved cereblon-dependent glues meet that standard for the induced-proximity mechanism, and the PROTAC arm inherits it because it exploits the same ternary-complex logic. On B067 as the fall-back, I agree that Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the cleanest chemistry, but the attribution against Rothberg, Mayer and Ju and the overlap with Physiology or Medicine make it a weaker lead than B026. I hold it as my first alternative.

uncertainties: My recollection of PROTAC clinical status, the approved glue drugs and the 2001 proof-of-concept history comes from memory, and no member has verified current trial status in this process. If a heterobifunctional degrader were to fail in late-stage trials, my confidence in the maturity argument would drop.
Whether the committee accepts that approved glue drugs justify recognising PROTACs before a first PROTAC approval; this is a judgment about standards and not a fact I can settle.
Whether leaving out Ciulli, Sakamoto and Kim can be defended in the reports, and whether the ternary-complex structural contribution ranks above Deshaies's early role in a strict reading.
Whether one citation can name induced proximity without implying a single discovery, and without reading as pharmacology.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. No conflict with any credited name on B026, B060 or B031. My field, nucleotide metabolism and ribonucleotide reductase, is close to the sequencing and base-editing alternatives (B067, B038) only in subject matter, and my Umeå and Cold Spring Harbor collaborators (Thelander, Stillman, Rothstein) are not credited on any shortlisted ballot.
